oil.summary: Crude staged a sharp intraday recovery — WTI +2.1% to $88.3/bbl, Brent +2.9% to $95.41 — but both benchmarks remain deep in the red on a one-month basis, having shed roughly 20% from late-October highs near $118/bbl. The rebound was largely geopolitically driven: Trump's declaration that the U.S. has no need for an Iran deal reversed earlier peace-optimism selling, briefly pushing Brent back above $96. Offsetting bullish pressure, Wednesday's EIA report showed a 4.7 mb crude build alongside gasoline and distillate builds, capping upside. On the supply side, UK sanctions on all ten of Russia's largest oil producers and shadow fleet vessels, combined with Ukraine's drone strikes reportedly cutting Russian refining capacity by 30%, add medium-term disruption risk. RBOB underperformed markedly (+0.4%), while heating oil (+1.7%) tracked crude more closely. CME options imply a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2027 meeting.
drivers: Trump rules out Iran deal, reviving geopolitical risk premium and briefly pushing Brent above $96
EIA reports a 4.7 mb crude build plus gasoline and distillate builds, capping the rally
UK sanctions Russia's ten largest oil producers and shadow fleet; Ukraine drone strikes cut Russian refining capacity ~30%

gas.summary: Henry Hub surged 4.6% on the day to $3.362/MMBtu, extending a sharp weekly gain of over 14%. The fundamental backdrop is tightening: Europe is entering winter with its lowest gas inventories of the 2020s, and Asian spot LNG is trading above $30/MMBtu, intensifying competition for cargoes. EU LNG imports from Russia have already exceeded full-year 2025 volumes with the bloc's January ban on Russian LNG still weeks away, underscoring the urgency to secure alternative supply. The combination of thin European storage, surging Asian demand, and the looming Russian LNG ban creates a structurally supportive environment for Henry Hub as U.S. LNG export demand increases. Domestic data flow was limited to the EIA crude report, which did not cover gas storage.
drivers: Europe enters winter with decade-low gas inventories, tightening global LNG balances
Asian spot LNG above $30/MMBtu intensifies competition with Europe for U.S. export cargoes
EU LNG imports from Russia already exceed 2025 totals ahead of the January ban, raising near-term supply replacement urgency

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up 1.8% to $85.42, holding constructively within a narrow one-month range (+2.1%). News flow for the sector today was varied but thin on direct carbon price catalysts. In the UK, Chancellor Healey's budget speech signalled a material shift in government positioning on net zero as soaring electricity costs force a rethink of green policy commitments. AI-driven data centre power demand continues to pressure U.S. grid infrastructure, with cost recovery questions increasingly pointed at ratepayers. Venezuela passed reforms opening its electricity sector to private capital for the first time since 2007, prioritising oil fields. Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain a tail risk for gas-fired power generation costs globally. Overall, carbon price action was modest and the broader news flow was more directionally relevant to medium-term demand than to today's EUA move.
drivers: UK government signals policy retreat on net zero amid soaring electricity costs
AI data centre power demand surge raising U.S. grid investment and cost-recovery questions
Iran's seven conditions for Hormuz reopening maintain geopolitical risk premium on gas-fired generation costs
